accuracy.evidence: Checked against AQA GCSE Physics (8463) 4.2.1.4: 'The resistance of a thermistor decreases as the temperature increases… The resistance of an LDR decreases as light intensity increases', with applications (thermostats; switching lights on when it gets dark), and 4.2.2 series circuits (total pd shared between components). Model values recomputed: LDR R = 20 kΩ × (10/E)^0.7 gives 32.5 kΩ, 6.48 kΩ, 1.29 kΩ, 258 Ω at 5, 50, 500, 5000 lux, inside the range of common CdS cells (e.g. GL5528: 8–20 kΩ at 10 lux, ≥1 MΩ dark). NTC 10 kΩ at 25 °C, B = 3950 K: 33.6, 10.0, 3.59, 1.49, 0.70 kΩ at 0/25/50/75/100 °C, matching typical datasheet tables within a few per cent. Divider on 6 V with 10 kΩ: V(LDR) 4.59/2.36/0.69/0.15 V; with the switch on the fixed resistor 1.41/3.64/5.31/5.85 V. Alarm trip points (V across fixed ≥ 3 V when R_fixed ≥ R_therm): 1 kΩ ≈ 88 °C, 3.6 kΩ ≈ 50 °C (3.00 V), 10 kΩ = 25 °C, 33 kΩ ≈ 0 °C. Parameterised answers checked at range corners by the items gate; divider items use whole-number shares so every answer is exact.

misconceptions.evidence: Targets documented errors (AQA examiner reports on 4.2.1.4 and potential dividers; IOP Supporting Physics Teaching: electric circuits): LDR backwards (more light, more resistance), thermistor treated like a metal wire, light 'not affecting' a resistor, resistance falling to zero, reading the wrong half of the divider, the sensor taking all the supply pd, the LDR's pd falling in the dark, choosing a bigger fixed resistor to delay an alarm, and changing the battery instead of the resistor. Each appears in a prediction, a lab message or challenge feedback.

lab_distinct.evidence: gate_lab_distinct passed under 30% against every flagship lab, including flag_ohm.js (V = IR), flag_circ.js (current and voltage), flag_series.js (circuit words), flag_cdiag.js (circuit diagrams) and flag_therm.js (thermometers). Only this lab plots sensor resistance against light and temperature, makes the learner choose which half of a divider a switch reads, tunes a fixed resistor to set an alarm's trip temperature, and sorts sensing devices.

lab_teaches.evidence: Six steps: slide light from dark to daylight and build the LDR graph point by point; heat a water bath 0–100 °C and build the thermistor graph; choose LDR or fixed resistor as the switch input and test dark and daylight (the wrong choice gives a lamp that is on by day); pick the fixed resistor so the alarm is quiet at 25 °C and rings at 50 °C (each wrong value reports its own trip temperature); sort six devices; then the challenge. Banners state the rule only after the task is done.

predictions.evidence: Three locked predictions with tempting wrong options the lab disproves: LDR into the dark ('it goes down'), a heated thermistor ('rises, like a metal wire'), and which part a night-light switch reads ('the fixed resistor', 'no difference'). The reveal names the learner's own choice after the task.

challenge_feedback.evidence: Six rotating questions with eleven distinct wrong-answer messages: LDR backwards, light has no effect, thermistor like a wire, resistance to zero, divider share backwards, sensor takes all the pd, two light-versus-temperature device mix-ups, bigger fixed resistor, bigger battery, and equal resistors sharing 0 V.

readability.evidence: learn/readability.py: kid text grade 4.5 and adult 4.9, inside 6.5 and 9.5. LDR is spelled out at first use; pd is introduced in plain words as voltage share. Canvas banners wrap to at most three lines at 360 px.

no_filler.evidence: gate_content found no filler patterns and the explanation is under 12% shingle overlap with 880 (Ohm's law), 525 (series and parallel) and 489 (electrical safety). Each kid paragraph does one job: LDR, thermistor versus wire, the night-light divider, the fire-alarm divider.

mobile.evidence: Screenshots at 360 × 640 (2x) in light and dark, before and after Show me, for all six steps. The first sheet showed the charts covering the live resistance readouts and the alarm labels colliding; charts were moved down, component names and values split onto two lines, and the trip temperature moved to a full-width line, and the second sheet shows every label clear. Slider knobs and component hit areas are at least 48 px.

accessibility.evidence: Every canvas drag or tap has a button twin (four light levels, five temperatures, switch reads LDR or fixed, Dark and Daylight, four resistor values, three temperatures, LDR and Thermistor). The canvas aria-label is rewritten after every action with the light level, temperature, resistance, which part the switch reads, the trip temperature and the current card. The browser gate ran axe (WCAG 2.1 AA) on desktop and iPhone 13 in both themes with no violations and no console errors.
